link.page: What's underneath the meltdown, a free tool for looking at what sits under your child's meltdowns

music.brief: Low steady pulse under a soft string pad, calm and focused, one gentle lift near the end, instrumental, for a short explainer video, about 60 seconds.

sources: Potegal & Davidson (2003). Temper Tantrums in Young Children: 2. Tantrum Duration and Temporal Organization. Journal of Developmental & Behavioral Pediatrics. 335 children, 18 to 60 months.

Wakschlag et al. (2012). Defining the developmental parameters of temper loss in early childhood: implications for developmental psychopathology. Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry. Nearly 1,500 preschoolers.

beats.text: It feels endless. The most common tantrum: 30 seconds to a minute.
beats.say: It feels endless, but the most common tantrum lasts a minute or less.

beats.sub: Anger first, then the part where your child needs you.
beats.say: And it has a shape, with a part where your child needs you.

beats.text: Parents of 335 children, 18 months to 5 years, described their tantrums.
beats.say: Parents of three hundred thirty five children described their tantrums.

beats.text: 3 in 4 tantrums were over within 5 minutes.
beats.say: Three in four were over within five minutes.

beats.text: How often nearly 1,500 preschoolers had tantrums
beats.say: Over eight in ten preschoolers had tantrums sometimes, and under one in ten daily.

beats.text: Out of nowhere, very long, or breaking things?
beats.sub: Or many a day for weeks? That is worth asking a pediatrician about.
beats.say: Tantrums that come from nowhere, go on and on, break things, or come many times a day for weeks are worth asking a pediatrician about.

beats.sub: The upset and crying build slowly underneath it.
beats.say: The anger came first and faded. The crying built slowly underneath.

beats.text: The honest catch: parents reported these times.
beats.say: The honest catch is that parents reported these times. Nobody used a stopwatch.

beats.text: Try this: stay close and quiet through the first minute.
beats.sub: When the crying turns to reaching for you, that is your moment to comfort.
beats.say: Try staying close and quiet through the first minute, when almost nothing reaches them. When they start reaching for you, comfort them.

beats.text: See what sits under the next meltdown.
beats.say: Our free tool, What's underneath the meltdown, is in the bio.
